so.subjective:
* Patient is a 54-year-old female who was referred to the doctor from the ER for esophagitis.
* The patient reports that the tests performed during their ER visit for chest pain three months ago did not reveal any abnormalities with their heart.
* The patient reports that the chest pain did not occur at the time of waking.
* She had chest pain a few months ago that lasted for four days and went away.
* The chest pain was sharp and located right behind her breastbone in the center of her chest.
* She also experienced difficulty swallowing during that time.
* She has not had any symptoms related to esophagitis since the initial episode three months ago.
* The patient states that the doctor mentioned an upper endoscopy as an option, but the patient chose to wait and see if symptoms worsen before pursuing it.
* The patient reports that cardiac stress testing and echocardiography were not performed subsequent to the initial evaluation due to the initial testing already ruling out cardiac causes of the prior chest pain.
* The patient reports that the EKG and blood tests performed during the ER visit did not reveal any cardiac issues, and the healthcare provider suspected a possible gastrointestinal issue instead.
* She does not smoke or drink alcohol and has been trying to lose weight.
* The patient reports that the blood tests performed during the ER visit showed normal results, but does not recall the exact names of the tests.
* She does not have a family history of cardiovascular disease.
* The patient reports feeling fine currently, but wants to ensure there is no underlying condition.
* The patient reports feeling better currently, but still desires reassurance that there are no other underlying issues.
* The patient reports wanting to ensure everything is okay.
